sentences.text: 1. Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 11.10.2019 passed in MVC No.486/2018 by the Court of the Senior Civil Judge and J.M.F.C., at Tiptur (for short 'the Tribunal'), the petitioners therein has preferred this appeal before the tribunal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
That on 05.11.2017 at about 7.00 p.m., the deceased Basavaraju was proceeding from his house towards K.B.Cross by pushing his cycle by walk and when he reached near the land of one Shashidhara near Kibbanahalli Tiptur Taluk, a TVS Star City Motor bike bearing registration No.KA-44-Q-7126 being driven in a rash and negligent manner and duly insured with respondent No.2 - insurance company came and dashed against the deceased, due to which he died.
Petitioner No.1 is his wife and petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are his children.
They preferred MVC No.486/2018.

The Tribunal, based on the evidence let in, has awarded a compensation of Rs.5,60,000/-
along with interest @ 9% p.a. under the following heads:-

The accident happened in the year 2017.
The deceased was aged about 55 years at the time of the accident.
He has not proved his income before the tribunal.

Hence, the income as per the lok adalat chart is taken at Rs.11,000/- per month and as per the decision laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in [2009(6) SCC 121] a multiplier of '11' is adopted.

Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680 future prospects of 10% is added to his income and 1/3rd is deducted towards his personal expenses.

sentences.text: Thus towards the 'loss of dependency' the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.10,64,800/- (11,000 x 12 x 11 x 2/3 +10%).
Towards 'funeral expenses' and 'loss of estate', the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.30,000/-.
Towards 'loss of consortium' the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each and thereby together they are entitled to a sum of Rs.1,20,000/- (40,000x3=1,20,000).

5. Thus, the compensation to the petitioners under different heads is modified as hereunder:-
 AMOUNT AMOUNT Sl. HEAD OF AWARDED BY AWARDED BY No. COMPENSATION THE TRIBUNAL THIS COURT  IN RS.

IN RS.
1 Love and affection 1,50,000-00 - 2 Loss of dependency 3,96,000-00 10,64,800-00  Funeral, obsequies and 3 14,000-00 30,000-00  transportation expenses 4 Loss of consortium - 1,20,000-00  5,60,000-00 12,14,800-00 6.

Thus, the petitioners are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.6,54,800/- (Rs.12,14,800/-
Rs.5,60,000/-).

Hence, the following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
ii. The total compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified and petitioners are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.6,54,800/- over and above what has been already awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition before the Tribunal till the date of realization.

iii. Respondent No.2 shall pay the enhanced compensation amount to the petitioners along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of the certified copy of the judgment and order.
